differences.text: Tecton links are body-coloured and the underline (on hover, or always with has-underline) is the only affordance: color=accent (the default) resolves to the primary text colour with no hover tint, as the owner's React theme re-points --color-text-accent for Link. primary and secondary keep upstream's 15% hover tint. The inner tct-text inherits the link colour so text, underline and icon always agree.

The router is not a component prop: tct-link-provider provides linkContext.navigate(href, event). A plain primary click on a same-origin link (not external, targeted, download or modified) is offered to it; returning true cancels the native navigation. Everything else stays native.
In forced colours the link takes LinkText (GrayText when disabled) instead of its palette colour, and the disabled dimming is dropped there.
With a tooltip active a host aria-describedby is not mirrored onto the inner control (tct-button does the same): the tooltip owns the description.

core.link.notes: Guides: [mwg:accessible-web-components] native a/button in the shadow root with delegatesFocus; [mwg:security] URL policy and noopener; [mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips] and [mwg:position-aware-tooltips] via TooltipController; [mwg:css] forced colours, hover only under (hover: hover). Utilities: useLinkify is the module function linkify() (linkify.ts); useLinkComponent is replaced by linkContext (tct-link-provider). Size: measured 46.71 kB gzip on 2026-09-29 (family entry with lit, core and the shared tooltip/layer/locale runtime inlined), budget 49 kB; revisit when the shared runtime is split out of family entries.

api.notes: A React component cannot be a prop of an element. The provider offers a navigation hook instead: navigate(href, event) => boolean, provided to every tct-link, link-form tct-button and tct-avatar link below it through linkContext. Read at click time.

differences.text: component (a React link component) is replaced by navigate (a click hook). Links stay native <a href>: plain primary clicks on same-origin destinations are offered to navigate, modified and middle clicks, new-tab links, downloads and cross-origin destinations stay native, and destinations refused by the URL policy never reach the router (they render without href), which covers upstream's useLinkComponent destination checks.
useLinkComponent has no equivalent hook: consumers of the router are the link elements themselves, through linkContext (core). Providers nest and the nearest wins.

requests.reason: runElementSuite's 'keeps its state across disconnect and reconnect' asserts element.shadowRoot is not null, which a light-DOM provider (ARCHITECTURE section 8: providers render nothing, no shadow root) can never satisfy. tct-link-provider repeats the suite's lifecycle checks itself. Proposed: a `shadow?: boolean` option (default true) that skips that one assertion.

core.link-provider.notes: Guides: [mwg:custom-elements] provider element without a shadow root; [mwg:security] URL policy stays in the link. Styling: tct-link-provider.light.css (display: contents in @layer tecton.light-dom) is delivered by the shared light-dom.css and cloak.css (@cloakDisplay contents) once those generators exist (M6); until then the element is a plain inline element in tests.
